### subset-b-009759: lines 1-7281

# sources/user-network-fs/rclone/cmd/bisync/testdata/bisync_vscode_debuggers_launch.json lines 1-7281

## Scope

This chunk covers the opening 7,281 lines of a generated VS Code `launch.json` fixture for rclone bisync debugging. The full source file has 59,189 lines, so this range is only the first slice. It starts at the JSON root with `"version": "0.2.0"` and `"configurations"`, then lists many Go test launch configurations for `./cmd/bisync`.

The chunk contains 909 complete launch entries with `args`, plus one trailing partial entry whose `name`, `type`, `request`, `mode`, and `program` are visible but whose `args` line is just outside the assigned range at line 7,282. The range is therefore not independently valid JSON; it must be reconciled with later chunks for whole-file parsing.

## Purpose

The file is developer testdata generated by `cmd/bisync/bisync_debug_test.go` to make bisync integration scenarios easy to launch under the VS Code Go debugger. Each object represents one debug configuration with:

- `"type": "go"`, `"request": "launch"`, and `"mode": "test"` for a Go test debug session.
- `"program": "./cmd/bisync"` so the debugger runs the bisync package tests.
- `"args"` equivalent to `go test ./cmd/bisync -- -remote <left> -remote2 <right> -case <testcase> -no-cleanup`.

The generator comment warns users to copy only selected entries into a real VS Code launch file because the generated full file is large enough to make VS Code crash.

## Data Shape And Represented APIs

The root object follows VS Code's launch schema:

- `version`: fixed at `0.2.0`.
- `configurations`: an array of debug configuration objects.

Every complete object in this chunk has the same fields and no optional debugger settings beyond the test arguments. The effective API surface represented by each entry is the bisync test harness CLI:

- `-remote`: first side of the bisync test.
- `-remote2`: second side of the bisync test.
- `-case`: one scenario directory under `cmd/bisync/testdata` whose name starts with `test_`.
- `-no-cleanup`: leaves generated test artifacts behind for debugger inspection.

The launch names encode the same dimensions as human-readable text: `Test <remote> <testcase> <variation>`, where variation is `LocalRemote`, `RemoteLocal`, or `RemoteRemote`.

## Coverage In This Chunk

The visible complete configurations cover 27 bisync scenario names:

`test_all_changed`, `test_backupdir`, `test_basic`, `test_changes`, `test_check_access`, `test_check_access_filters`, `test_check_filename`, `test_check_sync`, `test_compare_all`, `test_createemptysrcdirs`, `test_dry_run`, `test_equal`, `test_ext_paths`, `test_extended_filenames`, `test_filters`, `test_filtersfile_checks`, `test_ignorelistingchecksum`, `test_max_delete_path1`, `test_max_delete_path2_force`, `test_nomodtime`, `test_normalization`, `test_rclone_args`, `test_resolve`, `test_resync`, `test_resync_modes`, `test_rmdirs`, and `test_volatile`.

Backend coverage is ordered by the generator's backend list. This chunk includes:

- `local`: 27 names, only `RemoteRemote`, with both sides set to `local`.
- Ten full non-local backend groups with 81 names each: `TestB2:`, `TestCryptDrive:`, `TestCryptSwift:`, `TestChunkerLocal:`, `TestChunkerNometaLocal:`, `TestChunkerChunk3bLocal:`, `TestChunkerChunk3bNometaLocal:`, `TestChunkerChunk3bNoRenameLocal:`, `TestChunkerMailru:`, and `TestChunkerChunk50bMailru:`.
- A partial `TestChunkerChunk50bYandex:` group: 72 complete entries through `test_resync RemoteRemote`, then the visible start of `test_resync_modes LocalRemote` at lines 7,277-7,281.

For non-local backends, each testcase is normally expanded into three launch variants:

- `LocalRemote`: `-remote local -remote2 <backend>`.
- `RemoteLocal`: `-remote <backend> -remote2 local`.
- `RemoteRemote`: `-remote <backend> -remote2 <backend>`.

The line boundary explains why the first 24 cases have 34 complete `args` entries each in this chunk while the final three cases have only 31 complete `args` entries each.

## Generator Control Flow

`bisync_debug_test.go` drives this file:

1. `parseConfig()` reads `../../fstest/test_all/config.yaml` into `Config{Tests, Backends}` with `gopkg.in/yaml.v3`.
2. `generateDebuggers()` scans `b.dataRoot` and builds `testList` from non-empty directories whose names start with `test_`.
3. It iterates configured backends, defaulting an empty backend remote to `local`.
4. For every testcase, it loops over `LocalRemote`, `RemoteLocal`, and `RemoteRemote`.
5. For the `local` backend, it skips `LocalRemote` and `RemoteLocal` because those would duplicate `local` against `local`.
6. It formats each entry using `debugFormat`, wraps all entries with `docFormat`, and writes `./testdata/bisync_vscode_debuggers_launch.json` with `bilib.PermSecure`.

The JSON itself has no executable control flow; its behavior is entirely determined by VS Code's Go debugger and the bisync test harness that receives the command-line arguments.

## State And Persistence Behavior

This file is persistent generated testdata in the source tree. It does not mutate state at runtime. When used for debugging, each launch configuration can create or modify temporary bisync test directories, and `-no-cleanup` intentionally preserves those artifacts after the test run for inspection.

The represented bisync test runs are stateful because the selected testcase directories contain initial files, modified files, golden listings, golden queue files, and expected logs. The launch entry itself only selects the backend pair and test case; the actual state transitions are implemented by the bisync test harness and the scenario data under `cmd/bisync/testdata`.

## Dependencies And Integration Points

- `cmd/bisync/bisync_debug_test.go`: owns the generation logic, launch object format, and output path.
- `fstest/test_all/config.yaml`: supplies backend remotes used by the generator, although this fixture appears older or intentionally broader than the currently uncommented backend list because it still includes entries such as `TestCryptSwift:`, `TestChunkerMailru:`, `TestChunkerChunk50bMailru:`, and `TestChunkerChunk50bYandex:`.
- `cmd/bisync/testdata/test_*`: provides the testcase names and scenario contents selected by `-case`.
- VS Code plus the Go debug extension: consumes the `launch.json` shape and invokes Go test debugging.
- The bisync integration test harness: interprets `-remote`, `-remote2`, `-case`, and `-no-cleanup`.
- rclone remote configuration: remote names like `TestB2:` and `TestChunker...:` must exist in the developer's rclone config for those launches to run successfully.

## Risks And Maintenance Notes

- The generated file is very large. The generator explicitly warns that copying the whole file into a real VS Code launch file can crash VS Code.
- This chunk ends in the middle of a configuration object. Chunk-level tooling should not attempt to parse only lines 1-7,281 as complete JSON.
- The fixture may drift from `fstest/test_all/config.yaml` and from available remote definitions. The visible source config currently has some remotes in this chunk commented out, so regenerating from the current config may delete or reorder many entries.
- Testcase discovery depends on filesystem directory order as returned by `b.listDir`. Any ordering change in that helper or in generated testdata layout can rewrite large portions of this file.
- `-no-cleanup` is helpful for debugging but can leave local or remote artifacts behind, especially when a remote-backed configuration is launched accidentally.
- Every remote-backed launch assumes valid credentials, buckets, and backend-specific behavior. Missing remotes or stale test accounts produce debugger failures unrelated to bisync logic.
- The launch entries hard-code `./cmd/bisync`, so they are intended to run from the rclone repository root.

## Test Signals

Useful signals from this range:

- 27 local-only `RemoteRemote` entries at the top of the file.

## Purpose

This chunk is part of rclone bisync's generated VS Code debugger launch matrix. The file is produced by `cmd/bisync/bisync_debug_test.go` so developers can copy selected configurations into a real `.vscode/launch.json` and debug individual bisync integration-style test cases from VS Code.

The assigned range is not a standalone JSON document. It starts inside the `args` field for `Test TestChunkerChunk50bYandex: test_resync_modes LocalRemote` and ends inside the next object after `Test TestCompressSwift: test_rmdirs RemoteRemote`. The complete objects cover backend remotes from late `TestChunkerChunk50bYandex:` through most of `TestCompressSwift:`.

## Structure And Data Shape

Each complete entry follows the generator's fixed `debugFormat` shape:

- `name`: `Test <remote> <testcase> <variation>`.
- `type`: always `go`, selecting the VS Code Go debugger.
- `request`: always `launch`.
- `mode`: always `test`, so the Go extension launches a test binary rather than a normal program.
- `program`: always `./cmd/bisync`.
- `args`: always `["-remote", <path1>, "-remote2", <path2>, "-case", <testcase>, "-no-cleanup"]`.

The three debugger variations encode bisync side placement:

- `LocalRemote`: `-remote local`, `-remote2 <backend>`.
- `RemoteLocal`: `-remote <backend>`, `-remote2 local`.
- `RemoteRemote`: both sides use the same backend remote.

The complete objects in this chunk exercise the 27 bisync test-case directories generated from `b.dataRoot`: `test_all_changed`, `test_backupdir`, `test_basic`, `test_changes`, `test_check_access`, `test_check_access_filters`, `test_check_filename`, `test_check_sync`, `test_compare_all`, `test_createemptysrcdirs`, `test_dry_run`, `test_equal`, `test_ext_paths`, `test_extended_filenames`, `test_filters`, `test_filtersfile_checks`, `test_ignorelistingchecksum`, `test_max_delete_path1`, `test_max_delete_path2_force`, `test_nomodtime`, `test_normalization`, `test_rclone_args`, `test_resolve`, `test_resync`, `test_resync_modes`, `test_rmdirs`, and `test_volatile`.

## Covered Remotes

The line span is a contiguous slice through the backend loop from the generator. It contains:

- the last `TestChunkerChunk50bYandex:` entries for `test_resync_modes`, `test_rmdirs`, and `test_volatile`;

## Control Flow

There is no runtime control flow in the JSON testdata itself. The relevant control flow is in `bisync_debug_test.go`:

1. `parseConfig` reads `../../fstest/test_all/config.yaml` into `Config`.
2. `generateDebuggers` builds `testList` by scanning bisync testdata directories whose names begin with `test_` and are non-empty.
3. It iterates every configured backend, defaulting an empty backend remote to `local`.
4. For each backend/testcase pair, it iterates `LocalRemote`, `RemoteLocal`, and `RemoteRemote`.
5. It skips local-only duplicate variations when the backend remote is `local`.
6. It emits a fixed VS Code Go test launch object using `debugFormat`.
7. It writes the assembled document to `./testdata/bisync_vscode_debuggers_launch.json` with `bilib.PermSecure`.

This chunk is therefore a materialized product of backend order, discovered bisync test-case order, and the fixed three-variation loop.

## State And Persistence Behavior

The JSON file persists generated developer tooling state in the source tree under `cmd/bisync/testdata`. It is not read by bisync production code during synchronization.

Every launch entry includes `-no-cleanup`, which intentionally preserves test artifacts after a debug run. That is useful for inspecting path1/path2 listings, backup directories, lock files, and failure residue, but it means repeated manual debugging can leave remote-side or local-side state behind. Debuggers copied from this file should normally run against test remotes, not user data.

The generator overwrites the whole launch file when invoked. Manual edits to this generated testdata are not durable unless the generator or its config inputs are also changed.

## Dependencies And Integration Points

- VS Code's Go debug adapter consumes the object shape: `type: go`, `request: launch`, `mode: test`, and `program: ./cmd/bisync`.
- `cmd/bisync` test code consumes the command-line arguments, especially `-remote`, `-remote2`, `-case`, and `-no-cleanup`.
- `bisync_debug_test.go` depends on `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` for the backend config, `github.com/rclone/rclone/fs` for error logging, `github.com/stretchr/testify/assert` for write assertions, and `github.com/rclone/rclone/cmd/bisync/bilib.PermSecure` for output permissions.
- Backend remote names such as `TestChunkerS3:`, `TestCombine:dir1`, and `TestCompressSwift:` come from `fstest/test_all/config.yaml` and the user's rclone test configuration.
- The `-case` values integrate with bisync's test harness, selecting one testdata scenario at a time rather than running the full package test suite.

## Risks And Edge Cases

- The full file is not strict JSON as checked in: a direct `jq` parse fails because the generator leaves a trailing comma before the closing `configurations` array. VS Code may tolerate JSON-with-comments style syntax in `launch.json`, but strict JSON tooling will reject it unless the trailing comma is removed.
- The file is very large. The generator comment warns that VS Code can crash if all entries are copied into a real launch configuration. Developers should copy only the needed debugger object.
- The assigned chunk boundaries are not object-aligned. Any merge lane or research consumer must treat this file as a chunked generated artifact and not assume each chunk is independently parseable.
- Remote-to-remote entries use the same backend name for both sides. For backends without strong isolation, a copied debugger may need extra test-path scoping from the harness to avoid source/destination collisions.
- `-no-cleanup` is intentional for debugging but can accumulate state and affect later manual reruns if the harness or remote cleanup is not performed separately.
- Backend capability differences matter. This chunk concentrates on wrapper and object-storage remotes such as chunker, combine, compress, S3, Swift, and crypt-over-chunker paths; failures in modtime, checksums, empty directories, normalization, filters, or backup-dir behavior may be backend-specific rather than generic bisync defects.
- Because the file is generated from config and filesystem discovery, changes in backend order or testdata directory presence can cause large diffs with no semantic change to bisync itself.

## Test Signals

- Regenerating via the bisync debug generator should reproduce this matrix shape: fixed Go test launch entries with the same argument order and naming convention.
- A lightweight static check can confirm every complete object has `type = go`, `request = launch`, `mode = test`, `program = ./cmd/bisync`, and exactly the expected `args` flag sequence.
- Strict JSON parsing currently fails on the raw file; a permissive VS Code-oriented parse or a normalization step that removes the final trailing comma should be used when validating generated content with `jq`.
- Representative copied launch entries from this chunk should start a focused bisync test for backends such as `TestChunkerS3:`, `TestCombine:dir1`, and `TestCompressSwift:` with one of the three side-placement variations.
- Behavioral coverage comes from the selected `-case` scenarios: deletion limits, dry-run behavior, filters and filter-file checks, checksum-listing behavior, modtime-less backends, filename normalization, rclone argument forwarding, resync modes, directory removal, and volatile file handling.
- For generated-file regression tests, compare the set of emitted test cases and the three variation names rather than relying only on line numbers, because backend config changes can legitimately move this chunk's content.

## Important Data Shape

The object schema is uniform and generated by `bisync_debug_test.go`'s `debugFormat` template:

- `name` encodes the backend, test case, and variation in a human-readable VS Code picker label.
- `type` selects the VS Code Go debug adapter.

## Control Flow

There is no executable control flow inside this JSON file. The effective control flow is supplied by VS Code, the Go extension, and the bisync test harness:

1. A developer selects one launch configuration by `name`.
2. The Go debug adapter starts a Go test run for `./cmd/bisync`.
3. The test binary receives the listed flags.
4. `bisync_test.go` consumes `-remote`, `-remote2`, `-case`, and `-no-cleanup` via package-level `flag` variables.
5. The bisync test engine runs only the selected case against the selected pair of filesystem roots.

Within this chunk, the control-flow matrix is deliberately repetitive. For each complete backend block, the generated order is case-major: all three variants for `test_all_changed`, then all three for `test_backupdir`, and so on. That order mirrors the generator loops in `bisync_debug_test.go`: iterate backends, then test cases, then `LocalRemote`/`RemoteLocal`/`RemoteRemote`.

## State and Persistence Behavior

The JSON itself has no mutable state. The stateful effect comes from `-no-cleanup`, which tells the bisync test harness to retain temporary test files after the run. That is intentional for debugging because the selected launch target is meant to be run under an interactive debugger and the retained files help inspect failure state.

The remote flags choose where test fixtures and bisync metadata will be created. `local` uses local filesystem paths managed by the test harness. Named remotes such as `TestDrive:`, `TestDropbox:`, and `TestJottacloud:` rely on rclone integration-test remote configuration. `:memory:` uses rclone's in-memory backend and only persists for the process lifetime, although the launch entry still passes `-no-cleanup`.

Because every entry is a full independent debug launch, there is no persistent cursor or inter-entry dependency in this file. Persistence risks are external: leftover debug data on real remote providers, retained local temp directories, and provider-side objects that remain when tests fail or when `-no-cleanup` is used.

## Dependencies

The chunk depends on these repository components:

- `cmd/bisync/bisync_debug_test.go`, which generates `testdata/bisync_vscode_debuggers_launch.json` from backend, test-case, and variation lists.
- `cmd/bisync/bisync_test.go`, which defines and consumes the `-case`, `-remote2`, and `-no-cleanup` test flags alongside the primary `-remote` flag used by the rclone test framework.
- The VS Code Go extension's `launch.json` schema for `type: "go"`, `mode: "test"`, and package-relative `program` values.
- Rclone backend integration-test configuration for remotes such as Drive, Dropbox, Google Cloud Storage, Google Photos, HiDrive, ImageKit, Internet Archive, Jottacloud, and compressed-wrapper remotes.

The data also assumes that each named backend remote exists in the developer's rclone test configuration. Missing credentials, disabled integration remotes, quota limits, provider throttling, or backend-specific feature gaps will cause the selected launch entry to fail in the test harness, not in JSON parsing.

## Integration Points

The immediate integration point is VS Code debugger discovery: this file can be copied into or used as a source for `.vscode/launch.json` configurations. The generated entries are intentionally verbose so the debug picker exposes backend, case, and path-placement information without requiring the developer to inspect `args`.

The deeper integration point is the bisync test matrix. The `LocalRemote`, `RemoteLocal`, and `RemoteRemote` variants probe asymmetry in bisync behavior: local-to-remote, remote-to-local, and remote-to-remote setups can differ in modtime precision, checksum support, empty-directory support, case sensitivity, Unicode normalization, directory markers, object naming, and delete/copy semantics.

The compressed remotes (`TestCompressDrive:`, `TestCompressS3:`, and the tail of `TestCompressSwift:`) integrate bisync with rclone's compression wrapper layered over real backend providers. `TestGoogleCloudStorage,directory_markers:` is specifically useful for directory marker behavior, while `:memory:` is useful for fast, process-local behavior with different persistence semantics from cloud remotes.

## Risks and Edge Cases

- The chunk is not standalone JSON. It starts after an object's `name`/metadata fields and ends before a trailing object's `args`; tooling that validates only this line range as JSON will fail.
- The full launch file is huge. The generator warns that VS Code can crash if too many configurations are used at once, so this file is best treated as a catalog to copy from selectively.
- `-no-cleanup` is useful for debugging but risky against real integration remotes because failed or repeated runs can leave provider-side test data behind.
- Backend names are literal flag values. Colons, commas, and path suffixes such as `TestIA:rclone-integration-test` must not be normalized by downstream scripts.
- The `name` format is not completely uniform. Most remotes display as `Test <remote>: <case> <variant>`, while `TestIA:rclone-integration-test` appears without the extra colon separator. Parsers should prefer `args` over display names.
- The range's aggregate counts can be misleading because one leading entry contributes only `args`, and one trailing entry contributes only `name`/metadata. Merge tooling should use chunk boundaries from the manifest rather than infer completeness from local line counts.
- Real-provider launch entries are slow and may be flaky due to network, credentials, quotas, and backend consistency behavior. They should not be treated like deterministic unit-test launches.
- Direction variants using the same remote on both sides, such as `RemoteRemote`, may require the test harness to create distinct subpaths. A backend or remote configuration that maps both sides to the same physical path would invalidate the test.

## Test Signals

Useful validation signals for this chunk are structural and behavioral:

- Parse the entire `bisync_vscode_debuggers_launch.json` file as JSON, not this chunk alone, and confirm every configuration object has `name`, `type`, `request`, `mode`, `program`, and `args`.
- Regenerate the file from `go test ./cmd/bisync -run TestGenerateBisyncDebuggers` or the relevant generator test and compare this region for stable ordering and exact argument strings.
- For a representative complete backend block, verify there are 81 entries: 27 cases times three variants.

- Run a low-cost selected launch or equivalent command, such as a `:memory:` entry, to confirm the VS Code argument shape still maps to the bisync test flags.
- For real-provider entries, use targeted smoke tests rather than the full launch catalog because provider credentials and quotas are external to this file.

- `-remote2`: the second bisync path, defined in `bisync_test.go` as `argRemote2`.

There is no control flow in the JSON itself. The effective control flow appears when a developer selects one launch entry in VS Code:

## Purpose

`bisync_vscode_debuggers_launch.json` is a generated helper file for developers debugging individual bisync integration-test permutations in VS Code. It is not production code and does not implement bisync behavior. Each object is a Go debug configuration that launches tests in `./cmd/bisync` with a specific backend remote, a specific bisync fixture case, and one of three path topologies.

The generator is `generateDebuggers` in `cmd/bisync/bisync_debug_test.go`. It reads backend definitions from `../../fstest/test_all/config.yaml`, discovers fixture directories beginning with `test_`, and emits this file under `cmd/bisync/testdata`. The generator comment says developers should copy only needed entries into a real VS Code `launch.json`, because VS Code can crash if it loads too many configurations.

## Important Data Shape

Each complete launch configuration in this chunk has the same schema:

- `name`: human-readable label, for example `Test TestSeafile: test_basic LocalRemote`.
- `type`: always `go`, selecting the VS Code Go debugger integration.
- `request`: always `launch`.
- `mode`: always `test`, so the Go extension runs the target package as a test binary.
- `program`: always `./cmd/bisync`, the package containing the bisync tests.
- `args`: always `["-remote", <path1>, "-remote2", <path2>, "-case", <testcase>, "-no-cleanup"]`.

The topology encoded in `args` is:

- `LocalRemote`: `-remote local`, `-remote2 <backend>`.
- `RemoteLocal`: `-remote <backend>`, `-remote2 local`.
- `RemoteRemote`: both paths use the same backend remote.

The backend strings are rclone test remote names, not local filesystem paths. Most end with `:`, while SMB uses `TestSMB:rclone`, which includes a subpath after the remote name.

## Control Flow

The JSON file has no executable control flow. Runtime behavior comes from the VS Code Go extension and the Go test binary:

1. A developer chooses one copied configuration in VS Code.
2. VS Code launches the Go debugger in test mode for `./cmd/bisync`.
3. The test binary receives `-remote`, `-remote2`, `-case`, and `-no-cleanup`.
4. `bisync_test.go` binds those flags to test globals such as `argRemote2`, `argTestCase`, and `argNoCleanup`.
5. The bisync test harness runs only the selected fixture case against the selected path topology and leaves work files behind for debugging because `-no-cleanup` is set.

The generation flow is deterministic for a given backend config and fixture directory listing, but this chunk itself is static data.

## State And Persistence Behavior

The launch file persists developer/debug metadata in the repository under `cmd/bisync/testdata`. Running a configuration does not modify this JSON. The launched bisync test can create remote objects, local working directories, logs, listings, and retained test artifacts because every entry includes `-no-cleanup`.

State sensitivity is mostly in the external test remotes. Entries for Seafile, Sia, SMB, Storj, Zoho, HDFS, Oracle Object Storage, Quatrix, Ulozto, and related services assume the corresponding rclone test remotes are configured and reachable. `RemoteRemote` entries can exercise same-remote synchronization behavior and may require isolation in the test harness to avoid collisions.

Primary local integration points:

- `cmd/bisync/bisync_debug_test.go`: defines the `Config`, `Backend`, and `Test` structs for parsing `fstest/test_all/config.yaml`, plus the `debugFormat` and `docFormat` templates that generate this JSON.

- `fstest/test_all/config.yaml`: source of backend remote names and ordering.

External integration points are VS Code, the VS Code Go extension/debug adapter, Go test execution, and the configured rclone remotes named by the entries.

- The requested range starts mid-object, so this chunk alone is not standalone JSON. It must be interpreted as part of the full `bisync_vscode_debuggers_launch.json`.
- The file is very large. The generator explicitly warns that VS Code can crash if too many generated configurations are copied into a real launch file.
